question: Which of the following is known as ammonia?
solution:
The correct answer is** __NH____3.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nitrogen and hydrogen combine to form the **colorless**, smelly gas (NH3).
 
• It is the most basic stable compound of these elements and is used as a raw material to create a variety of nitrogen compounds with significant industrial applications.
 
• Ammonia has the** chemical formula NH3 **and is a colorless gas.
 
• **Nitrogen and hydrogen make up its composition**.
 
• Its name in aqueous form is ammonium hydroxide.
 
• Ammonium Hydroxide, Ammonium Conjugate, Azanide Conjugate, Ammonia Solution, Strong, and Ammonium (Conjugate) (related).
 
• Total **ammonia (NH3), free ammonia (NH4+), and ammonium** are the three different forms of ammonia (NH3).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NH3:**

 
 
• Aqueous ammonia or liquid ammonia are two names for this type of ammonia.
 
• Ammonia gas forms quickly when liquid ammonia is exposed to the atmosphere.** **
 
• **Ammonia **is used to manufacture fertilizers for farm crops, lawns, and plants, and it is injected directly into the soil on agricultural fields.
 
• **Ammonia is a common ingredient in commercial and domestic cleansers.**
 
• Ammonia is created by **human activity and occurs naturally**.
 
• It is a significant supply of nitrogen, which both plants and animals depend on.
 
• Ammonia can be produced by** intestinal bacteria**.
 
• The colorless gas known as ammonia has a **potent aroma**.
 
• Because ammonia is a common ingredient in window cleaners, household and industrial cleaners, and smelling salts, many people are familiar with this stench.
 
 
 
• **PH3**:
 
 
• The naturally occurring **anaerobic degradation of organic materials** containing phosphorus results in the formation of phosphonate, an extremely **poisonous phosphorus hydride**.
 
• It can also be manufactured through an alkali metal hydroxide or white phosphorus hydrolysis event.
 
• Phosphine is employed as a **pesticide,** in industrial operations, and in the creation of flame retardants.
 
• When pure, it is described as an **odorless, colorless gas.** Inhalation, ingestion, or touch all result in exposure.
 
 
 
• **NO3**:
 
 
• **​**With the chemical formula **NO3, nitrate is a polyatomic ion**.
 
• This** ion** is found in** salts**, which are known as **nitrates**.
 
• Fertilizers and explosives frequently contain nitrates as a component. 
 
• About all **inorganic nitrates are water soluble**.
 
• Bismuth oxynitrate is an illustration of an insoluble nitrate.
 
 
 
• **NO2**:** **
 
 
• **​**The chemical compound with the formula** NO is nitrogen dioxide**.

 It belongs to a group of nitrogen oxides.
 
• Millions of tonnes of nitric acid are produced annually for use largely in fertilizer manufacture, with NO serving as an intermediary in this process.
 
• When the **temperature rises, the gas turns reddish-brown**.
 
• If inhaled in significant amounts, it can be **letha**l.
 
• A bent, **paramagnetic molecul**e with C2v point group symmetry is nitrogen dioxide.
